metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (PHP 8.2) with a deployable entry point (index.php served via Apache), a Dockerfile, and AWS CloudFormation IaC provisioning App Runner and RDS.
metadata.archetype_justification: Database connections with full CRUD operations (orders, inventory, payments, returns, users), customer-specific data (user sessions, order history), and entity lifecycle management (order status workflow).

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith — all domains in single PHP file with shared MySQL database
top_gaps.impact: Blocks independent scaling, deployment, and team autonomy

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipeline — all deployments manual via bash script
top_gaps.impact: Prevents rapid iteration, quality gates, and safe automated releases

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.gap: No automated tests of any kind in the repository
top_gaps.impact: No regression safety net; all changes carry full-system risk

top_gaps.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
top_gaps.gap: No messaging infrastructure — all state changes synchronous within monolith
top_gaps.impact: Tight coupling between domains; no event-driven decoupling

top_gaps.title: Async vs Sync Communication
top_gaps.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns
top_gaps.impact: Creates cascading failure risk when decomposed

findings.title: Workflow orchestration is hardcoded in application logic
findings.description: Multi-step order fulfillment workflow (confirm→validate→warehouse→pick→pack→QC→ship→deliver) implemented entirely as hardcoded state transitions in PHP route handlers with no dedicated orchestration service.
findings.gap: Multi-step business-critical workflows hardcoded in application code with no retry logic, error handling strategy, or visual workflow management.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the fulfillment workflow with built-in retry logic, error handling, and audit trail.

findings.title: No messaging infrastructure for cross-domain state changes
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. All state changes crossing domain boundaries are handled in single synchronous database transactions. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, MSK, or Kinesis.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries — tight synchronous coupling between domains that should be decoupled.
findings.recommendation: Introduce Amazon EventBridge or SQS for cross-domain event propagation starting with order lifecycle events.

findings.title: Network security lacks VPC endpoints for private AWS service access
findings.description: Services in private subnets with least-privilege security groups and VPC Flow Logs. WAF protects entry point. However, no VPC endpoints or PrivateLink configured.
findings.gap: No VPC endpoints for AWS service access — traffic to ECR, CloudWatch traverses internet rather than private connectivity.
findings.recommendation: Add VPC endpoints for ECR, CloudWatch Logs, and other AWS services accessed from the VPC.

findings.title: API entry point lacks granular API management
findings.description: App Runner with WAF provides basic entry point with IP whitelisting and managed rules. No API Gateway with per-route throttling, request validation, or usage plans.
findings.gap: No API Gateway with request validation, throttling per-route, or usage plans.
findings.recommendation: Introduce Amazon API Gateway as the unified entry point when decomposing into microservices.

findings.title: Auto-scaling limited to compute layer only
findings.description: App Runner auto-scaling configured (min 1, max 3, MaxConcurrency 100). RDS db.t3.micro has no auto-scaling — fixed instance with no read replicas or storage auto-scaling.
findings.gap: Auto-scaling coverage limited to compute with no scaling on data layer.
findings.recommendation: Consider Aurora Serverless v2 for automatic database compute scaling or enable RDS storage auto-scaling.

findings.title: Backup configuration lacks cross-region replication and restore testing
findings.description: RDS automated backups with 7-day retention, deletion protection, and snapshot-on-delete. No cross-region backup replication or documented restore testing.
findings.gap: No cross-region backup replication. No documented restore testing procedure.
findings.recommendation: Enable cross-region automated backups. Document and test restore procedures. Consider AWS Backup for centralized management.

findings.title: IaC coverage missing operational and monitoring resources
findings.description: CloudFormation covers VPC, subnets, RDS, App Runner, ECR, WAF, IAM, security groups, KMS, VPC Flow Logs (70-90% coverage). Missing CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, and SNS topics.
findings.gap: No CloudWatch alarms, dashboards, or monitoring resources defined in IaC.
findings.recommendation: Extend CloudFormation to include CloudWatch alarms, SNS notification topics, and dashboards.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline — all deployments manual
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployments are entirely manual via bash script (docker-compose) for local dev and manual CLI commands for production (build, ECR push, CloudFormation update).
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages. No quality gates or automated rollback.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline using AWS CodePipeline with CodeBuild: source → build → push to ECR → deploy to App Runner.

findings.title: PHP language limits cloud-native tooling depth
findings.description: PHP 8.2 with no framework — raw procedural PHP with PDO. No composer.json or dependency manifest. Limited cloud-native tooling ecosystem compared to Python, Go, Java, or TypeScript.
findings.gap: PHP has functional AWS SDK but limited cloud-native tooling depth. No framework limits structured patterns.
findings.recommendation: When decomposing, consider migrating extracted services to languages with deeper cloud-native ecosystems. If PHP retained, adopt Laravel or Symfony.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries
findings.description: Single PHP file (~2000+ lines) containing all business domains: orders, inventory, payments, returns, warehouse, users, fulfillment. Shared MySQL database with cross-table foreign keys. No module boundaries.
findings.gap: No clear module boundaries. Pervasive shared state. Cannot scale, deploy, or evolve domains independently.
findings.recommendation: Decompose using Strangler Fig approach. See Decomposition Strategy for extraction order and patterns.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All domain interactions are synchronous in-process calls and direct database queries. Order creation executes inventory check, order insert, inventory deduction, and payment in single synchronous transaction.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns. Creates cascading failure risk when decomposed.
findings.recommendation: Introduce event-driven communication with Amazon EventBridge for order lifecycle events and SQS for return processing.

findings.title: All operations synchronous regardless of duration
findings.description: Fulfillment workflow requires multiple sequential manual API calls with no background processing. Return processing takes 24-48 hours of manual review with no async status tracking.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background job infrastructure. No async status tracking.
findings.recommendation: Implement async job processing with Step Functions for fulfillment workflow and SQS workers for return processing.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: All endpoints use unversioned paths (/api/products, /api/orders, /api/returns). No version prefix, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — any API change breaks all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL-path versioning (/v1/) consistently across all endpoints.

findings.title: Environment variables for endpoints but no dynamic discovery
findings.description: Database host configured via DB_HOST environment variable injected by CloudFormation. No dynamic service discovery mechanism.
findings.gap: No dynamic service discovery. Will not scale when decomposed into multiple services.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS Cloud Map or API Gateway as service registry when decomposing.

findings.title: No object storage for unstructured data
findings.description: No S3 usage. All data in MySQL tables. Product images referenced by URL paths but no actual storage infrastructure. No document parsing capability.
findings.gap: Data on local/inaccessible storage. No S3 bucket or managed object storage configured.
findings.recommendation: Store product images and documents in S3 with CloudFront for delivery. Enables future AI document intelligence.

findings.title: Database queries scattered with no abstraction pattern
findings.description: Raw SQL statements scattered throughout route handlers. Over 50 $db->prepare() and $db->query() calls with no repository/DAO layer. Only get_db() and update_order_status() as reusable functions.
findings.gap: No data access pattern. No abstraction layer between business logic and database queries.
findings.recommendation: Introduce repository/DAO layer per domain before decomposition to create natural service boundaries.

findings.title: Database versions pinned but no update procedure documented
findings.description: MySQL 8.4.8 explicitly pinned in CloudFormation (current, not EOL). AutoMinorVersionUpgrade enabled. Docker-compose uses MySQL 8.0 for local dev (version mismatch).
findings.gap: No documented version-update procedure. Dev (8.0) and prod (8.4.8) use different versions.
findings.recommendation: Document version update procedure. Align development with production MySQL version.

findings.title: RDS uses AWS-managed encryption rather than customer-managed KMS
findings.description: RDS StorageEncrypted: true with AWS-managed key. ECR and VPC Flow Logs use customer-managed KMS keys with rotation. RDS lacks customer-managed key.
findings.gap: RDS uses AWS-managed encryption. Limited control over key policy and rotation.
findings.recommendation: Create customer-managed KMS key for RDS. Document encryption strategy with key hierarchy.

findings.title: Session-based authentication without token-based auth
findings.description: PHP session-based authentication with bcrypt password hashing. All API endpoints check $_SESSION['user']. WAF provides IP-based access control. No OAuth2/JWT.
findings.gap: No token-based authentication. Session-based auth is stateful and unsuitable for multi-service or agent communication.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to JWT via Amazon Cognito for stateless auth across decomposed services and AI agent integration.

findings.title: Application manages authentication independently with no IdP
findings.description: Users table stores credentials internally. Login, user creation, and role management handled within the monolith. No Cognito, OIDC/SAML, or external IdP.
findings.gap: No external IdP integration. No SSO. Identity siloed in application database.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito. Migrate users table to Cognito user pool for SSO, MFA, and federated identity.

findings.title: No secrets management — credentials in environment variables without rotation
findings.description: Database credentials passed via CloudFormation NoEcho parameters as App Runner environment variables. No Secrets Manager. No rotation. PHP source has development fallback defaults.
findings.gap: No secrets management service. No rotation. Production credentials in plaintext environment variables.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Remove development fallback defaults from source.

findings.title: Default base image without hardening or dependency scanning
findings.description: Standard php:8.2-apache image. Non-root user and read-only filesystem configured. ECR ScanOnPush enabled. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no Dependabot/Renovate.
findings.gap: Default image without hardening. No dependency scanning pipeline. ECR scan results have no blocking gate.
findings.recommendation: Adopt hardened base image. Configure Dependabot/Renovate for base image updates. Integrate ECR scan into CI/CD gate.

findings.title: No application security scanning in pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured in any pipeline (no pipeline exists). No Dependabot, SAST, or container scanning gate. ECR ScanOnPush is reactive with no blocking behavior.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. No pipeline to integrate security validation.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (Semgrep), container image scanning gate, and dependency scanning in the CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No distributed tracing instrumented
findings.description: No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or tracing SDK. No trace ID propagation. App Runner supports X-Ray but it is not configured.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Debugging cross-service flows impossible when decomposed.
findings.recommendation: Enable X-Ray on App Runner. Instrument each decomposed service with OpenTelemetry SDK.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms. Basic App Runner health checks only. RDS Enhanced Monitoring provides database metrics but no application-level SLOs.
findings.gap: No formal definition of acceptable service levels. Cannot measure system performance against expectations.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical user journeys. Implement CloudWatch alarms for latency, error rate, availability.

findings.title: No business metrics published
findings.description: No custom metrics. No CloudWatch PutMetricData. Only default App Runner and RDS infrastructure metrics available.
findings.gap: No custom metrics. Cannot measure business outcomes or modernization impact.
findings.recommendation: Instrument business metrics: orders_placed, fulfillment_cycle_time, return_rate. Publish to CloudWatch.

findings.title: No alerting configured
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms (static or anomaly-based). No notification integration. No automated failure detection.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures detected only via user reports or manual checks.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for 5xx error rate, latency p99, RDS metrics. Configure SNS notifications.

findings.title: Rolling deployments without traffic shifting
findings.description: App Runner rolling deployments with health check validation. No canary, blue/green, or traffic-shifting capability.
findings.gap: Rolling deployments with basic health checks but no traffic shifting for progressive validation.
findings.recommendation: Configure App Runner traffic splitting for canary-style deployments or adopt blue/green when migrating to ECS/EKS.

findings.title: No automated tests of any kind
findings.description: No unit tests, integration tests, or end-to-end tests. No test directories, frameworks, or configuration. No PHPUnit, Pest, or API test collections.
findings.gap: No integration tests. Changes carry full-system regression risk. Cannot safely extract services.
findings.recommendation: Establish integration test suite for critical workflows. Run tests in CI pipeline before deployment.

findings.title: No incident response automation or runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no SSM Automation documents, no Lambda-based remediation, no Step Functions for incident workflows. Incident response entirely ad hoc.
findings.gap: No runbooks. Incident response entirely ad hoc with no documented procedures.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents. Start with markdown, then automate with SSM Automation documents.

findings.title: No observability ownership defined
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS. No service-level dashboards. No alarms with named owners. No team attribution on resources.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. Monitoring reactive and fragmented with no accountability.
findings.recommendation: Define observability ownership: CODEOWNERS file, per-service dashboard, team tags on resources.

findings.title: Resource tagging lacks standard and enforcement
findings.description: Most resources have Name tags. ECR and App Runner have Environment tags. No cost allocation, ownership, or service identification tags. No enforcement.
findings.gap: No consistent tagging standard beyond Name. Missing CostCenter, Team, Service tags. No enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Define tagging standard with required keys. Implement AWS Config required-tags rule for enforcement.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: All compute on App Runner (fully managed container service). No EC2.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: RDS MySQL fully managed with Multi-AZ, automated failover, encrypted storage.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: RDS Multi-AZ, App Runner inherently multi-AZ, VPC Connector spans 2 AZs.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: No stored procedures or proprietary SQL. All business logic in application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Application-level IaC only. CloudTrail is account-level, belongs in foundation infrastructure repo.
